dedupe_keys.name: vehicle connectivity and dynamic traffic response to unplanned urban events

description: The source describes initial offline microsimulations in the Turin Living Lab, considering street, lane and intersection closures along autonomous-shuttle routes. It varies connected and connected-autonomous vehicle penetration and compares dynamic rerouting. Higher connectivity improves traffic flow in the reported tests. The Living Lab combines simulation and real-world testing, but the stated paper findings concern the offline phase and are not treated as measured effects of live incident response. The source authors provide the native description and file descriptors through Zenodo. Only metadata was inspected; no measurements, archives, source code or document bodies were retrieved. Public access and the deposit document licence do not establish executable access, software reuse rights or operating costs. Coverage remains bounded to the named experiments, with other geographic and temporal fields unknown. Related project resources may overlap; common project membership does not establish identical simulation inputs or results.
name: Vehicle Connectivity and Dynamic Traffic Response to Unplanned Urban Events
